name: Balance Protocol BTCB spot-poke unbacked mint and withdrawal
summary: Balance Protocol's permissionless BTCB price path accepted a manipulated price with no validation: the oracle wrapper and Spotter poke calls refreshed the stored price and filed it into Vat, and Vat.frob then authorized unbacked BLC debt minting and BTCB collateral withdrawal against the false spot. GemJoin and BlcJoin exits paid the attacker directly, and PancakeSwap and SmartRouter swaps realized the proceeds in USDT.
notes: Directly deployed Vat accounting runtime created by the protocol deployer. No proxy code-selection path and no pre-exploit code change; the exploitable price-spot combination completed when the oracle and Spotter deployments joined it in the same launch campaign.

Directly deployed Spotter-style price-relay runtime created by the protocol deployer. Its permissionless poke entry filed the manipulated BTCB price into Vat with no deviation, floor, or delay check. No proxy code-selection path and no pre-exploit code change.

Directly deployed OSM-style oracle wrapper created by the protocol deployer, completing the oracle-to-Spotter-to-Vat combination. Its permissionless poke entry refreshed the stored BTCB price consumed same-transaction with no freshness or manipulation resistance. No proxy code-selection path and no pre-exploit code change.

Exact pre-recovery victim depletion from pool payout legs in the three same-fault campaign transactions: 52833.890793109591603470 plus 708862.704903208386296283 USDT in the anchor, 14927279434726129096 plus 93633807309981979623697 plus 28496315975075951166290 wei across three pool payouts in the second transaction, and 2123087448775227454826 wei from the PancakeSwap pair in the third. The attacker supplied no campaign inputs besides gas: no BTCB entered GemJoin before the anchor withdrawal, so the full 10.737 BTCB exit is victim collateral. Sub-dollar dust transfers and the actors' later unrelated activity are excluded.
Not the knot: one link of the conjunctive failure; the sibling with the latest age reset supplies the incident's single observation.

Three same-fault legs merge into this one incident anchored on the earliest exploit; the second and third actors repeat the identical oracle-poke, Spotter-poke, Vat-frob, exit, and swap sequence against the same code.
